title: Maximum overshadowing of an adjoining property (Table 3.9a)
text: In climate zones 4, 5, and 6, development is designed that its shadow cast at midday, 21 June (refer Figure 3.9a) onto any other adjoining property and/or diagonally adjacent lot (refer Figure 3.9b) does not exceed the limits set out in Table 3.9a.

exceptions.label: C3.9.2 single storey, wall height not more than 3.5 m
C3.9.3 narrow adjoining lot (R40+, frontage 7.5 m or less): Table 3.9b governs

replaces.note: percentages unchanged; R80+ adjoining now no maximum; diagonal lots now covered at R40 and below
'R50 or higher 50%' -> R50-R60 50%, R80+ no maximum

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 2 - Single Houses.pdf

notes: Shadow as % of the adjoining site area measured at NGL. Dividing fences up to 2 m do not contribute (Figure 3.9c). Where the adjoining site is a grouped dwelling development the limit applies per dwelling site excluding common property (footnote 1; adjoining.south.is_grouped_site, not encoded). C3.9.2 exemption also requires the single-storey building to meet C3.2.1, C3.4.1, C3.4.5, C3.4.6 (which does not exist in Chapter 2) and C3.1.1 (no metric at R30+); only storeys and wall height are tested. Named codes have no Table 3.9a row and return NOT_APPLICABLE (R80 standards). Coding excludes R100-SL: Table 2.10a removes all 3.9 provisions for R100-SL, but its footnote restores them where the development abuts a property not coded R100-SL (not encoded).

verified.note: Table 3.9a and C3.9.2 checked on p42-43. C3.9.2 exception tests storeys and wall height only (the cross-referenced C3.2.1, C3.4.1, C3.4.5, C3.4.6, C3.1.1 are not tested; exception keeps its own verify flag).
